originalTitle: Suryoday SFB Q1 profit more than doubles on strong loan growth
simplifiedContent: Suryoday Small Finance Bank just announced that it made a lot more money in the first quarter of the year, with its profit jumping to 75 crore rupees. This is because the bank had strong growth in the loans it gave out, which helped increase its income. The bank also saw improvements in other areas, such as its operating profit and the quality of its loans. This is good news for the bank and its investors, as it shows that the bank is doing well and growing its business. Overall, the bank's strong performance is a positive sign for its future.

originalTitle: Dow forecasts quarterly core profit slightly above estimates, warns of Middle East uncertainty
simplifiedContent: Dow Inc, a chemical company, thinks it will make a bit more money than expected in the third quarter of the year. This is because the company has been good at cutting costs, and its packaging and specialty plastics business is doing well. However, the company is also warning that there might be some challenges ahead, and it's also worried about what's happening in the Middle East. Despite these concerns, the company's stock price went up a bit after they announced this news. This matters because it gives investors an idea of how the company is performing and what to expect in the future.

originalTitle: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Friday
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in the stock market: the main Indian stock indexes, Sensex and Nifty, have been going down for four days in a row. This is because oil prices are rising and there's tension between the US and Iran, which is making investors nervous. As a result, investors are worried that prices might keep going up (inflation) and the market might keep being unpredictable (volatile). Analysts think the Nifty index will have a hard time going above 24,000 due to these concerns. This matters because it could affect how your investments perform on Friday.

originalTitle: Yen’s Slump Extends Beyond Dollar and Stokes Inflation Fears
simplifiedContent: The value of the Japanese yen has been falling, not just against the US dollar, but against other currencies as well. This means that the yen is worth less than it used to be, which is a big deal because it's been happening for a while now. The yen has fallen to its lowest point in 40 years against the dollar, and this trend is causing concerns about inflation. Inflation is when prices for goods and services rise, making the money in your pocket worth less. This matters because it can affect the overall economy and potentially impact your investments.

originalTitle: Dollar hits new 40-year high versus yen, euro softer after ECB stands pat on rates
simplifiedContent: The value of the US dollar has reached its highest point against the Japanese yen in 40 years. This means that the dollar can be exchanged for more yen than it could before. At the same time, the value of the euro (the currency used by many European countries) has gone down slightly. This happened after the European Central Bank (ECB) decided not to change interest rates, which was a decision that affected the value of the euro. This matters because it can impact international trade and investments, and may influence the decisions of people and businesses who buy or sell currencies.

originalTitle: Gold falls 2% as Middle East tensions fuel inflation fears, rate-hike bets
simplifiedContent: The price of gold dropped by 2% recently. This happened because of rising tensions in the Middle East, which is causing people to worry about inflation (prices rising too quickly). When people worry about inflation, they think that interest rates might go up to control it. As a result, investors are selling gold, which is why its price is falling. This matters to investors because a drop in gold price can affect their investments and the overall stock market.
